sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry confirmed surface display of myc-MuSK-GFP in BaF3 cells (L2); construct was used in functional cell-adhesion assays testing Lrp4-MuSK interaction (L3); adhesion assay result not explicitly quantified in the ledger clips but construct was employed as a functional reagent.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the myc tag was placed between the second and third Ig-like domains of full-length MuSK in a membrane-anchored retroviral construct. No specific residue number is given in the ledger, so insert_after_residue is left null and the site is reported at region level (Ig2-Ig3 linker, approximately the junction between UniProt-annotated Ig-like domain 2 ending ~211 and Ig-like domain 3 starting ~212, well within the extracellular span 24-495 and far from the TM boundary at 496). L2 and L3 confirm surface display by flow cytometry and use in functional adhesion assays, respectively, supporting surface_and_function validation. Full-length myc-MuSK-GFP expressed via retroviral vector in myoblasts and BaF3 cells; myc epitope inserted between the second and third Ig-like domains of MuSK (citing Herbst and Burden, 2000). Surface display confirmed by flow cytometry (L2); construct used in functional Lrp4-MuSK adhesion assays (L3).

sources.claim: The myc epitope tag was positioned between the second and third Ig-like domains in MuSK ( Herbst and Burden, 2000 ); the Flag epitope tag was positioned twenty four amino acids following the initiator methionine in Lrp4.
Accordingly, we inserted a streptavidin-binding sequence (SBP), called SBP-Tag, into the extracellular domain of MuSK.

literature_notes: L1, L2, and L3 all describe the same myc-MuSK-GFP construct; L1 is the primary positional evidence (names the Ig2-Ig3 linker), L2 and L3 add surface and functional validation. The GFP moiety in myc-MuSK-GFP is fused to the intracellular C-terminus (residue 869 region) and is recorded in other_positions as an intracellular tag. L4 describes a separate SBP-Tag insertion in the extracellular domain with no sub-region named; it qualifies as a distinct site but with low positional resolution. No ledger line names a specific residue for either insertion, so both sites are region-level with insert_after_residue null. No ledger line supports a terminal_n tag (mature N-terminus, residue 24) or a terminal_c tag (C-terminus is intracellular). No ledger line reports a function-abrogating insertion in the extracellular domain.

literature_other_positions.note: GFP fused to the C-terminus of myc-MuSK-GFP; the MuSK C-terminus (residue 869) is intracellular (topology: 517-869), so this fusion is cytoplasmic and not a surface tag site.
